bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sector concentration in real estate and tourism — The Company states that the risks it faces in its business principally arise from the Real Estate and Tourism industry, so earnings are tied to a single cyclical demand pool rather than diversified across sectors.
- Macroeconomic risk — Explicitly listed among the principal risks; managed through investment decisions based on third-party research and internal assessment. Travel and hospitality demand is discretionary and turns with the economic cycle.
- Investee-company-specific risk — Named as a principal risk alongside macroeconomic risk, covered by investment decisions based on third-party research and internal assessment - indicating exposure to the performance of entities the Company is invested in.
- Market-wide liquidity risk — Listed as a principal risk; management says market-wide risks are assessed and managed through investment timing decisions.
- Execution risk relating to the Company and its intermediaries — Named as a principal risk; managed by dealing with reputed intermediaries and through own back-office discipline in accounting and follow-up of trades.
- Cost inflation compressing operating margins — Inflationary pressures on food, energy and employee costs, rising compliance requirements and increasing investment in technology and sustainability are flagged as pressures on operating margins.
- Competition from new hotel supply and alternative accommodation platforms — Intensifying competition from alternative accommodation platforms and new hotel developments is flagged as a threat to the industry.
- Demand shock from geopolitical events, global slowdown and travel disruption — Geopolitical uncertainties affecting international travel, fluctuations in foreign tourist arrivals and a global economic slowdown may hit travel sentiment and discretionary spending; the industry also remains vulnerable to pandemics, natural disasters, adverse weather and transport-network disruption.

outlook.body:
- Continued focus on operational efficiency and prudent cost management initiatives
- Operational discipline, efficient resource utilisation and effective cost optimisation to improve profitability on broadly stable revenue
- Conserving resources and strengthening the financial position for future growth opportunities, in place of a dividend payout for the year
- Inducting competent personnel as and when activity increases or expands, with human resources reviewed periodically by management
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
- Indian hospitality demand supported by robust domestic tourism, increasing business travel, MICE, destination weddings, religious tourism and improving international tourist arrivals
- ICRA projecting 6-8% revenue growth for the Indian hospitality industry during FY 2025-26, with the premium hotel segment expected to sustain occupancy of 72-74% and ARRs improving to Rs 8,200-8,500 on demand outpacing supply
- UN Tourism projecting international tourist arrivals to increase 3%-4% in 2026 on sustained consumer demand, expanding airline capacity and major global sporting events
- Sector investment by domestic and international hotel chains, expansion into Tier-II and Tier-III cities and growth in branded hotel inventory, supported by government tourism-infrastructure initiatives, improved connectivity and rising disposable incomes
- Industry adoption of digital technologies - artificial intelligence, automation and data analytics - to lift operational efficiency and personalise guest experience
- Sustainability initiatives and a consumer shift towards experiential travel seen as creating new growth opportunities
- Margin headwinds flagged: inflationary pressure on food, energy and employee costs, rising compliance requirements, and increasing technology and sustainability investment
- Demand-side risks flagged: geopolitical uncertainty affecting international travel, fluctuations in foreign tourist arrivals and a global slowdown weighing on discretionary spending

litigation.note: A long-running ground-rent dispute with the Delhi Development Authority over the Company's property at Plot No. A-2, 3 & 4, District Centre, Wazirpur, Delhi: following DDA show-cause notice and a later demand, the Company twice filed writ petitions in the Delhi High Court; the court stayed DDA's order subject to a deposit, which the Company made, and the matter remains pending for final disposal, with management stating the liability will be determined only after disposal. Read in the contingent-liabilities note carried under the related-party transactions block of the bundle. The same note also lists a claim against the company not acknowledged as debt and a bank guarantee. Separately, the Board's Report states that no significant material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals during the year impacting going-concern status.
